items.title: The Next Target for Data Breach Lawsuits – Law Firms That Represent Breached Parties
items.summary: Mark Rasch writes: Imagine a company gets hacked and hires a law firm to manage the response. The lawyers coordinate the forensic investigation, determine which notification laws apply, and advise management about what to disclose and when. Months later, the notices arrive. The affected individuals sue the company and add its lawyers as defendants. Their...

items.title: NI: Parents warned to be on alert after school data breach
items.summary: Robbie Meredith reports: Parents have been told to be alert for unexpected emails or phone calls after a Northern Ireland school app used by almost 50,000 people was affected by a data breach. The Equipple app is used by many schools to schedule and book meetings between parents and teachers. There have been concerns that...

items.title: DigiCert data breach exposes customer information, identity documents
items.summary: Lawrence Abrams reports: DigiCert warns it suffered a data breach after a server migration mistakenly exposed an internal business system to the internet, allowing unauthorized access to customer information and identity documents. The certificate authority says the breach affected a small portion of its archived customer data, including names, business email addresses, phone numbers, and...

items.title: Any long password will do: SSH flaw lets hackers into Alpine systems, routers and more
items.summary: Ernestas Naprys reports: A massive decade-old flaw affects Alpine and other distributions that run OpenSSH on the musl library. Containers, routers, IoT devices, and other applications are critically vulnerable. Emergency updates are available. Any long password, between 257 and 1024 characters, unlocks thousands of Linux systems via SSH (Secure Shell), the industry standard for remote...

items.title: UK: Royal Cornwall Hospitals Trust data breach exposed health details of 7,715 staff
items.summary: Lee Trewhela reports: The Royal Cornwall Hospitals Trust (RCHT) has admitted a huge data breach has led to many affected staff experiencing “significant distress, loss of trust and ongoing anxiety”. The breach exposed sensitive personal health information relating to almost 8,000 current and former staff. An Excel spreadsheet published in February 2023 exposed hidden sickness...

items.title: Anthropic won’t fix a Claude Dispatch flaw that could let attackers execute remote commands across corporate boundaries
items.summary: Jessica Lyons reports: A vulnerability in Anthropic’s Claude products lets any browser extension that can control Claude Dispatch make Claude Desktop run code on the computer – or even a different machine signed into the same Claude account – with no browser exploit and minimal user interaction required. Anthropic, aware of the problem since May,...
